record.paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
record.original_question: Let l be a positive continuous function of one complex variable, and say that an entire function has bounded l-index if finitely many normalized derivatives |f^(k)(z)|/(k! l(z)^k) dominate all normalized derivative orders at every z. If f(z) has bounded l-index and w is an entire solution of the infinite-order linear differential equation sum_{k=0}^infty a_k w^(k)(z) = f(z), what assumptions on the coefficients a_k and on f(z) guarantee that w also has bounded l-index?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $l:\mathbb{C}\to(0,\infty)$ be a positive continuous function. An entire function $g:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ is said to have bounded $l$-index if there exists a non-negative integer $N$ such that for every $z\in\mathbb{C}$,
$$\frac{|g^{(N)}(z)|}{N!\,l(z)^{N}}\;\ge\;\max_{0\le k\le N}\frac{|g^{(k)}(z)|}{k!\,l(z)^{k}}\;\ge\;\frac{|g^{(k)}(z)|}{k!\,l(z)^{k}}\quad\text{for all }k\ge 0,$$
and the least such $N$ is the $l$-index of $g$.

Let $\{a_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of complex numbers (or, more generally, entire functions), and let $f$ be an entire function of bounded $l$-index. Consider an entire solution $w$ of the infinite-order linear differential equation
$$\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} a_k\, w^{(k)}(z) \;=\; f(z),\qquad z\in\mathbb{C}.$$

Determine sufficient conditions on the coefficients $\{a_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ (for instance, conditions on their growth or decay, on the radius of convergence of $\sum a_k\zeta^k$, or on majorization by $l$) and on $f$ which guarantee that every such entire solution $w$ also has bounded $l$-index.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of identifying conditions on coefficients of infinite-order linear differential equations that guarantee bounded l-index of solutions appears to remain open. Known results address finite-order equations, polynomial/rational coefficient cases (Lepson, and subsequent work on vector-valued bounded-index solutions), and special bounded-L-index settings, but no general criterion for the infinite-order case with bounded l-index data is reported in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Vector-Valued Entire Functions of Bounded Index Satisfying a Differential Equation
status_evidence.snippet: If F is a solution of F'=AF+Q with A,Q having rational entries bounded at infinity, then components of F are of bounded index.
status_evidence.claim: Existing results treat finite-order systems with rational coefficients; the infinite-order l-index question is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Differential equations, infinite-order system of - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: General theory of infinite-order differential equations.
status_evidence.claim: General theory exists but does not provide bounded l-index criteria for solutions.

status_evidence.title: Logarithmic derivative and zeros of an entire function of bounded ℓ-index
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of bounded l-index entire functions.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational results on bounded l-index, but the infinite-order ODE problem remains an open question.
